AbstractText.Label: INTRODUCTION
AbstractText.content: Both the overall shape of the calcaneus and anatomical reduction of joint congruity are important prognostic factors. However, there is a significant lack of biomechanical data supporting the clinical importance of calcaneus height, length and heel width. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of abnormal calcaneus morphology on ankle-hindfoot biomechanics.

AbstractText.Label: HYPOTHESIS
AbstractText.content: The normal biomechanics of the ankle-hindfoot would be severely disrupted by the abnormal calcaneus morphology.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Fifteen human cadaveric feet were evaluated intact and post-osteotomy after application of a 20N load. The kinematics of the ankle-hindfoot were compared between normal and simulated calcaneal fractures with reductions in calcaneal height, widening of the heel and shortening of the calcaneal length. In finite element analysis, static loading was simulated at an axial load with the subtalar joint in a neutral position, and the effects of the injured calcaneus on the contact characteristics of the subtalar joints were evaluated in terms of the contact areas, peak contact pressures and pressure distributions.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The increases in calcaneal width somewhat limited subtalar motion, and the reductions in length mainly limited external rotation and plantar flexion of the subtalar joint. However, the reductions in height mainly resulted in subtalar rotatory instability. The increases in width somewhat broadened the contact area but more notably increased the high-pressure contact zone. With height loss, the overall contact area decreased, and the contact pressure center shifted to the anteroinferior portion of articulation. However, the contact pressure peak remained almost constant.

AbstractText.Label: DISCUSSION
AbstractText.content: The normal biomechanics of the ankle-hindfoot were severely disrupted by the abnormal calcaneus morphology, and reestablishment of the geometric parameters of the calcaneus could restore the relative positions of the 3 superior calcaneal facets and minimize subtalar pain associated with the development of arthrosis and stiffness. Therefore, the 3D calcaneus anatomy should be carefully restored in patients with no risk factors.
